region.name: Colorado
region.setting: A box matching the state of Colorado: the Rocky Mountains, where the Colorado, Rio Grande, Arkansas and South Platte rivers rise, and the high plains to the east.

variable.name: Air temperature
variable.definition: Average air temperature two meters above the ground, about head height.

verdict.title: Significant rising trend that holds across date ranges
verdict.text: Over 1981-2025 the series changed by +0.326 °C per decade. Both significance tests agree after allowing for month-to-month persistence, and 95% of all date windows of 15+ years point the same way.

crosscheck.label: Supported by a second dataset
crosscheck.text: NASA GISTEMP v4, an independent record, shows +0.259 °C per decade (95% range +0.153 to +0.365): also significant, and its range overlaps this one.

dataset.name: NASA GISTEMP v4
dataset.long_name: NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4, 1200 km smoothing, land and ocean
dataset.kind: Weather-station and ship/buoy measurements interpolated onto a 2° grid, as differences from 1951–1980.
dataset.native_grid: 2° latitude x 2° longitude, smoothed over 1200 km
dataset.citation: GISTEMP Team (2026). GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4. NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies. https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/. Lenssen, N., et al. (2019). Improvements in the GISTEMP uncertainty model. J. Geophys. Res. Atmos., 124(12), 6307-6326.
dataset.caveat: GISTEMP spreads each station's signal over up to 1200 km, so a regional value blends in its surroundings. Agreement is support, not proof.

provenance.api_title: NASA/POWER Source Native Resolution Monthly and Annual

source.dataset: MERRA-2 (Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2)
source.producer: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO)
source.access: NASA POWER Monthly and Annual API (NASA Langley Research Center)
source.kind: Reanalysis: a global model constrained by satellite and ground observations. Values are model-based estimates, not direct instrument readings.
source.caveat: MERRA-2 is a reanalysis: a model constrained by satellite and ground observations, not a direct measurement. Changes in the observing system over time (new satellites, fewer rain gauges) can create or hide trends, especially for precipitation and soil wetness. Check important results against an independent dataset.
source.credit: NASA GMAO MERRA-2 via NASA POWER
